rubric.why: Electron transfer is the defining feature of redox reactions.
rubric.description: State that electrons are transferred between molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying electron transfer between molecules, not just mentioning oxidation or reduction alone.

rubric.why: The electron flow in redox reactions helps generate energy as ATP in cellular processes.
rubric.description: Link redox reactions to ATP/energy generation in metabolism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting electron flow or redox reactions with ATP production or energy generation in cellular respiration or photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons between molecules and are fundamental to metabolism.
This electron flow helps generate energy in the form of ATP during cellular respiration and photosynthesis.

rubric.why: The full forms distinguish the nucleotide ATP from the product ADP.
rubric.description: Give the meanings of ATP and ADP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying ATP as adenosine triphosphate and ADP as adenosine diphosphate.

rubric.why: ATP and ADP transfer energy between energy-releasing and energy-consuming metabolic reactions.
rubric.description: Explain ATP's role in cellular metabolism as an energy carrier, including its conversion to ADP or energy transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP breakdown to ADP releases energy, or that ATP transfers energy between metabolic reactions.

modelAnswer: ATP is adenosine triphosphate; when its outer high-energy bond breaks, it becomes ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and releases energy.
ATP is made in energy-releasing processes and broken down in energy-consuming processes, transferring energy between metabolic reactions.

rubric.why: Pigments, especially chlorophyll, absorb sunlight to initiate photosynthesis.
rubric.description: State that chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying light absorption by chlorophyll or photosynthetic pigments; mention of blue and red wavelengths is acceptable but not required.

rubric.why: Absorbed light excites electrons, whose energy supports formation of ATP and reduction of NADP to NADPH.
rubric.description: Explain how absorbed light is converted into chemical energy, such as ATP and NADPH formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking absorbed light or excited electrons to ATP and NADPH production, or to conversion into chemical energy.

modelAnswer: Pigments absorb sunlight and convert it into chemical energy for photosynthesis; chlorophyll-a absorbs blue and red light.
Light-excited electrons pass through an electron transport chain, providing energy for ATP formation and the reduction of NADP to NADPH.

rubric.why: Light splits water during photosynthesis, releasing oxygen.
rubric.description: State that light breaks water molecules and oxygen is released.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying light-driven water splitting as the source of released oxygen.

rubric.why: Hydrogen atoms donate electrons to chlorophyll and become hydrogen ions.
rubric.description: Describe the fate of hydrogen during water splitting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hydrogen atoms give electrons to chlorophyll and become hydrogen ions.

modelAnswer: Light breaks water molecules during photosynthesis, releasing oxygen.
Hydrogen atoms give electrons to chlorophyll and become hydrogen ions.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis is carried out by autotrophs, including plants, algae and some bacteria.
rubric.description: Identify the organisms that carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming autotrophs or giving suitable examples such as plants, algae or some bacteria.

rubric.why: The light reactions take place on the thylakoid membranes inside chloroplasts.
rubric.description: Name the cell structure where the light reactions occur.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts.

modelAnswer: Autotrophic organisms, including plants, algae and some bacteria, carry out photosynthesis.
The light reactions take place on the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts.

rubric.why: The defining condition for aerobic respiration is the presence of oxygen.
rubric.description: Define aerobic respiration by its oxygen condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cellular respiration in the presence of oxygen is aerobic respiration.

rubric.why: The defining condition for anaerobic respiration is the absence of oxygen.
rubric.description: Define anaerobic respiration by its oxygen condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cellular respiration in the absence of oxygen is anaerobic respiration.

modelAnswer: Cellular respiration occurring in the presence of oxygen is called aerobic respiration.
Cellular respiration occurring in the absence of oxygen is called anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Anaerobic respiration in animal skeletal muscles converts pyruvic acid into lactic acid.
rubric.description: Give the end product of anaerobic respiration in animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying lactic acid as the animal end product.

rubric.why: In yeast, pyruvic acid is broken down into alcohol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: Give the end products of anaerobic respiration in yeast.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying alcohol (ethanol) and carbon dioxide as the yeast end products.

modelAnswer: In animals, anaerobic respiration converts pyruvic acid into lactic acid (C₃H₆O₃).
In yeast, pyruvic acid is broken down into alcohol (C₂H₅OH) and CO₂.

rubric.why: During intense exercise, the oxygen supply may not meet the muscles' demand.
rubric.description: State the condition that triggers the muscle response.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inadequate oxygen supply relative to the muscles' demand during hard work or exercise.

rubric.why: When oxygen is insufficient, skeletal muscles carry out anaerobic respiration to obtain energy.
rubric.description: State the response of muscles to oxygen deficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that muscles perform anaerobic respiration to get energy.

modelAnswer: When skeletal muscles work hard during exercise and their oxygen supply is insufficient to meet demand, they carry out anaerobic respiration to obtain energy.
